The total thermal resistance per unit area is the sum of the convective resistances and the conductive resistances of the eight layers:

- Inside convective resistance: \(R_{\text{conv,i}} = 1/10 = 0.1\ \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W}\)
- Layer 1 (stone): \(R_1 = 0.28/2.3 \approx 0.121739\)
- Layer 2 (glass wool): \(R_2 = 0.04/0.04 = 1.0\)
- Layer 3 (concrete): \(R_3 = 0.24/1.4 \approx 0.171429\)
- Layer 4 (clay): \(R_4 = 0.075/1.1 \approx 0.068182\)
- Layer 5 (gypsum board): \(R_5 = 0.02/0.17 \approx 0.117647\)
- Layer 6 (wood): \(R_6 = 0.01/0.13 \approx 0.076923\)
- Layer 7 (plywood): \(R_7 = 0.015/0.12 = 0.125\)
- Layer 8 (gypsum board): \(R_8 = 0.075/0.17 \approx 0.441176\)
- Outside convective resistance: \(R_{\text{conv,o}} = 1/17 \approx 0.0588235\)

Total resistance \(R_{\text{total}} \approx 2.28092\ \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W}\).  
The temperature difference is \(\Delta T = 20 - (-2) = 22\ \text{K}\).  
Heat flux \(q = \Delta T / R_{\text{total}} \approx 9.64523\ \text{W/m}^2\), which rounds to \(9.645\ \text{W/m}^2\) to four significant figures.

The cumulative resistance from the inside air to the interface between layers 4 and 5 is:  
\(R_{\text{up}} = R_{\text{conv,i}} + R_1 + R_2 + R_3 + R_4 \approx 1.46135\ \text{m}^2\cdot\text{K/W}\).  
The temperature drop to that interface is \(\Delta T_{\text{up}} = q \times R_{\text{up}} \approx 14.0951\ \text{K}\).  
Thus the interface temperature is \(T_{\text{interface}} = 20 - 14.0951 = 5.9049\ \text{°C}\), which rounds to \(5.905\ \text{°C}\) to four significant figures.
